slides.title: Radha's fruit cart equation
slides.kicker: Mangoes, bananas, and one neat equation
bullets: Radha buys some kilograms of mangoes at 60 rupees per kg and some kilograms of bananas at 50 rupees per kg, paying 280 rupees in all.
We do not know either quantity, so let x be the number of kilograms of mangoes and y the number of kilograms of bananas.
The mangoes cost 60x rupees and the bananas cost 50y rupees, so the total is 60x + 50y = 280.
The LHS and the RHS both represent the same quantity, the total cost in rupees.
slides.note: Do unknowns se hi poora equation ban gaya!

slides.title: Standard form of these equations
slides.kicker: One costume every linear equation can wear
bullets: Any equation that can be written as ax + by + c = 0, with a and b not both zero, is a linear equation in two variables.
Here a is the coefficient of x, b is the coefficient of y, and c is a constant.
For 5x + 2y - 2.7 = 0 we read a = 5, b = 2, c = -2.7; multiplying by -1 gives a = -5, b = -2, c = 2.7, and both are valid.

items: a and b not both zero

slides.title: Clearing fractions from equations
slides.kicker: Fractions allowed, but integers are comfier
bullets: The coefficients and the constant may be rational numbers, so (1/4)x + (3/5)y - 2 = 0 is already a linear equation in two variables.
For convenience, we multiply the equation by a suitable number to remove the fractions.
Multiplying by 20 turns (1/4)x + (3/5)y - 2 = 0 into 5x + 12y - 10 = 0, the same equation with integer coefficients.
slides.note: Fractions wale equation ko 20 se multiply karo, sab integer!

slides.title: When y goes missing
slides.kicker: One visible variable, still two variables
bullets: Equations like ax + c = 0 are special cases of linear equations in two variables: write them as ax + 0 times y + c = 0.
For example, 7 + 4x = 0 can be written as 4x + 0 times y + 7 = 0, with a = 4, b = 0 and c = 7.
The only rule is that a and b are not both zero at the same time, so one of them may happily be zero.

slides.title: What counts as a solution
slides.kicker: A pair that makes the equation true
bullets: A solution of a linear equation in two variables is a pair of values of x and y which satisfy the given equation.
For 3x + 2y = 12, the values x = 2 and y = 3 work because (3 times 2) + (2 times 3) = 12.
The pair x = 4 and y = 0 also works, since (3 times 4) + (2 times 0) = 12.
But x = 1 and y = 3 gives 9, which is not 12, so the pair (1, 3) is not a solution.

slides.title: Order matters in pairs
slides.kicker: (2, 3) and (3, 2) are different
bullets: A solution can be written compactly as a pair of numbers, for example the solution x = 2, y = 3 is written as (2, 3).
The order of the numbers in this pair matters: the first number is the x-value and the second number is the y-value.
That is why we call it an ordered pair; swapping the order describes a different pair of values altogether.

slides.title: Endless solutions, one equation
slides.kicker: Pick any x, cook up its y
bullets: For any value u that we assign to x, we can find a value v for y such that the pair (u, v) is a solution.
Substitute u for x first; the equation becomes a new linear equation in y alone, which we can solve to find v.
Since u can be chosen freely, this process generates an infinite number of solutions to the original equation.

items: Choose any value u for x
Solve the resulting equation in y

slides.title: Solutions draw a straight line
slides.kicker: Plot every solution, get one line
bullets: Rewrite 3x + 2y = 12 as 2y = -3x + 12, which is the same as y = (-3/2)x + 6, the y = mx + d form met in the Linear Polynomials chapter.
Plotting solution points A (-1, 7.5), B (0, 6), C (1, 4.5) and D (4, 0) shows them joining into one straight line.
Every solution of the equation is a point on the line, so the line is the geometric picture of all the solutions.
slides.note: Saare solutions ek seedhi line par khade hain!

slides.title: Steepness has a name
slides.kicker: From cycling uphill to slope
bullets: On a flat road you can move without much effort, but as a road becomes steeper you have to work harder to climb it.
In mathematics, this idea of the steepness of a line is called its slope, or gradient.
A positive slope means going upward as we move from left to right; a negative slope means going downward.

slides.title: Rise over run
slides.kicker: Two steps: across, then up
bullets: The horizontal distance between two points is x2 - x1, called the Run; moving right gives a positive run, moving left a negative run.
The vertical distance is y2 - y1, called the Rise; going up makes the rise positive, going down makes it negative.
The slope of a line is Rise over Run, that is (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).

slides.title: Computing a slope
slides.kicker: A (2, 0) to B (4, 3), step by step
bullets: Take a line through the points A (2, 0) and B (4, 3).
Point B is reached from A by moving 2 units along the positive x-direction, the run, and 3 units along the positive y-direction, the rise.
Hence the slope of the line is Rise over Run = 3/2.

slides.title: Same line, same slope
slides.kicker: Any two points agree on steepness
bullets: Extend the same line AB further beyond B and pick different pairs of points on it.
Each pair of points gives the same value of rise over run, because the steepness of one straight line never changes.
So the slope belongs to the whole line, not to the two points you happened to choose.

slides.title: A puzzle made of shapes
slides.kicker: Triangles, rectangles, circles as unknowns
bullets: In the shape puzzle, 2 triangles and 2 rectangles add up to 28, so 2T + 2R = 28, which is the same as T + R = 14.
The last column gives 2C + T + R = 22, where T, R and C are the values of the triangle, rectangle and circle.
Since T + R = 14, the second equation becomes 2C + 14 = 22, giving C = 4; then you can find the other shapes too.

items: Use T + R = 14 to get C = 4

slides.title: Two equations, one goal
slides.kicker: Shrink a pair to one variable
bullets: To solve a pair of linear equations, we look for methods that reduce the pair to a linear equation in one variable.
The book studies two such algebraic methods: the method of substitution and the method of elimination.
Both paths end at the same place: one equation, one unknown, one clean value.

slides.title: Substitution in three steps
slides.kicker: One equation donates x, the other receives
bullets: Step 1: pick one equation, say x + 2y = 3, and express one variable in terms of the other: x = 3 - 2y.
Step 2: substitute this into the other equation, 7x - 15y = 2, giving 7(3 - 2y) - 15y = 2.
The pair has collapsed into one equation in y alone, which is exactly the reduction we wanted.

slides.title: Finishing and verifying
slides.kicker: Fractions in the answer are fine
bullets: The substitution gives 21 - 14y - 15y = 2, so -29y = -19 and therefore y = 19/29.
Put y = 19/29 back into x = 3 - 2y to get x = 3 - 38/29 = 49/29.
The solution is x = 49/29 and y = 19/29; verify it by substituting the pair into both original equations.

slides.title: Solving by drawing lines
slides.kicker: Each equation becomes a line
bullets: To solve a pair graphically, prepare a table of values with at least two ordered pairs for each equation.
Plot the points on the Cartesian plane and draw the straight line through each set of points.
The solutions of the pair are exactly the points that lie on both lines.

slides.title: Three ways lines meet
slides.kicker: One point, none, or all of them
bullets: When the two lines intersect in a single point, the pair has a unique solution, that one common point.
When the two lines are parallel, they share no point at all, so there are no solutions.
When the two lines are coincident, every point is common, so there are infinitely many solutions.
slides.note: Do lines kabhi cross karte hain, kabhi nahi!

slides.title: Example 11: build the tables
slides.kicker: Two equations, four friendly points
bullets: For x + 3y = 6, write y = (6 - x)/3; choosing x = 0 and then 6 gives y = 2 and 0, so (0, 2) and (6, 0) are points on the line.
For 2x - 3y = 12, write y = (2x - 12)/3; choosing x = 0 and then 3 gives y = -4 and -2, so (0, -4) and (3, -2) are points on the line.
Plot A (0, 2), B (6, 0), P (0, -4) and Q (3, -2) on graph paper, and join the points to form the lines AB and PQ.

slides.title: Where the lines cross
slides.kicker: The common point is the answer
bullets: We observe that the point B (6, 0) is common to both the lines AB and PQ.
In fact the lines AB and PQ intersect at B, so the solution of the pair is x = 6 and y = 0.
Because the lines meet in exactly one point, the given pair of equations has a unique solution.
slides.note: Point B hi asli hero, dono lines ka common point!

flashcards.front: What is the standard form of a linear equation in two variables?
flashcards.back: ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero.

flashcards.front: In ax + by + c = 0, what do a, b and c represent?
flashcards.back: a is the coefficient of x, b is the coefficient of y, and c is a constant.

flashcards.front: Mangoes cost 60 rupees a kg, bananas 50 rupees a kg, total 280 rupees. What equation fits?
flashcards.back: 60x + 50y = 280, with x the kilograms of mangoes and y the kilograms of bananas.

flashcards.front: Multiply (1/4)x + (3/5)y - 2 = 0 by a suitable number to clear fractions. What do you get?
flashcards.back: Multiplying by 20 gives 5x + 12y - 10 = 0, the same equation with integer coefficients.

flashcards.front: What is a solution of a linear equation in two variables?
flashcards.back: A pair of values of x and y which satisfy the given equation.

flashcards.front: Why is (1, 3) not a solution of 3x + 2y = 12?
flashcards.back: Substituting gives 3 times 1 + 2 times 3 = 9, which is not 12, so the equation is not satisfied.

flashcards.front: In the ordered pair (2, 3) for an equation in x and y, which number is which?
flashcards.back: The first number is the x-value and the second is the y-value; the order matters.

flashcards.front: How many solutions does a linear equation in two variables have?
flashcards.back: Infinitely many: for any value u of x you can solve for a matching value v of y.

flashcards.front: What shape do you get when you plot all solutions of a linear equation in two variables?
flashcards.back: A straight line; every solution (x, y) is a point on that line.

flashcards.front: What is the slope of a line?
flashcards.back: A measure of the steepness of the line, also called its gradient.

flashcards.front: State the slope formula for a line through A (x1, y1) and B (x2, y2).
flashcards.back: Slope = Rise over Run = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).

flashcards.front: What does a positive slope tell you about a line, reading left to right?
flashcards.back: The line goes upward as we move from left to right; a negative slope goes downward.

flashcards.front: A line passes through A (2, 0) and B (4, 3). What is its slope?
flashcards.back: The run is 2 and the rise is 3, so the slope is 3/2.

flashcards.front: In the shape puzzle, 2C + T + R = 22 and T + R = 14. What is C?
flashcards.back: Substitute T + R = 14 to get 2C + 14 = 22, so C = 4.

flashcards.front: What is the goal when solving a pair of linear equations algebraically?
flashcards.back: Reduce the pair to a single linear equation in one variable, using substitution or elimination.

flashcards.front: In Example 7, which expression for x is used to substitute into 7x - 15y = 2?
flashcards.back: x = 3 - 2y, obtained by expressing x in terms of y from x + 2y = 3.

flashcards.front: Two graphed lines intersect at exactly one point. How many solutions does the pair have?
flashcards.back: Exactly one: the unique solution is the single common point of the two lines.

flashcards.front: What happens to the solution count when the two lines are parallel or coincident?
flashcards.back: Parallel lines give no solutions; coincident lines give infinitely many solutions.
The lines meet at B (6, 0), so x = 6 and y = 0 is the unique solution.

quiz.q: Radha buys x kg of mangoes at 60 rupees per kg and y kg of bananas at 50 rupees per kg, paying 280 rupees in all. Which equation fits?
quiz.why: Mangoes cost 60x and bananas cost 50y, and both add up to the total 280.

quiz.q: In the standard form 5x + 2y - 2.7 = 0, what is the value of c?
quiz.why: c is the constant term, and moving 2.7 to the left side makes it -2.7.

quiz.q: Writing 7 + 4x = 0 in the form ax + by + c = 0 gives which values of a, b and c?
quiz.why: It becomes 4x + 0 times y + 7 = 0, so the coefficient b of y is zero.

quiz.q: Multiplying (1/4)x + (3/5)y - 2 = 0 by a suitable number to remove the fractions gives:
quiz.why: Multiplying every term by 20 gives 5x + 12y - 10 = 0 with integer coefficients.

quiz.q: Which ordered pair is a solution of 3x + 2y = 12?
quiz.why: (2, 3) gives 6 + 6 = 12, while the others give 9, 13 and 10.

quiz.q: How many solutions does a linear equation in two variables have?
quiz.why: For any value u of x you can solve for a matching v of y, so solutions never run out.

quiz.q: When you plot all the solutions of 3x + 2y = 12 on the plane, what picture appears?
quiz.why: Points like (2, 3), (4, 0) and (0, 6) join into one straight line.

quiz.q: Given 3x + 2y = 12 and a chosen value u for x, how do you find the matching value v of y?
options: Substitute u for x, then solve the resulting linear equation in y
Substitute u for y, then solve for x
Add u to both sides of the equation
quiz.why: Substituting u for x leaves a linear equation in y alone, which is solved for v.

quiz.q: In mathematics, the idea of the steepness of a line is called its:
quiz.why: The book calls the steepness of a line its slope, or gradient.

quiz.q: Which formula gives the slope of a line through A (x1, y1) and B (x2, y2)?
quiz.why: Slope = Rise over Run, with rise = y2 - y1 and run = x2 - x1.

quiz.q: A line passes through A (2, 0) and B (4, 3). Its slope is:
quiz.why: From A to B the run is 2 and the rise is 3, so slope = 3/2.

quiz.q: In the shape puzzle the last column gives 2C + T + R = 22, and you know T + R = 14. What is C?
What is the first step of the substitution method for the pair x + 2y = 3 and 7x - 15y = 2?
options: Write x = 3 - 2y from the first equation
Write x = 3 + 2y from the first equation
Set x equal to y and solve
quiz.why: Pick one equation and express one variable in terms of the other, here x = 3 - 2y.

quiz.q: In Example 7, substituting x = 3 - 2y into 7x - 15y = 2 leads to which value of y?
quiz.why: The working gives 21 - 29y = 2, so -29y = -19 and y = 19/29.

quiz.q: Two graphed lines intersect at exactly one point. The pair of equations has:
quiz.why: Solutions are points on both lines, and one intersection point means one solution.

quiz.q: Two graphed lines are parallel. How many solutions does the pair of equations have?
quiz.why: Parallel lines never meet, so no point lies on both lines.

quiz.q: Solving x + 3y = 6 and 2x - 3y = 12 graphically, at which point do the lines AB and PQ intersect?
quiz.why: B (6, 0) is common to both lines; the other points lie on only one line each.

examples.title: Writing equations in standard form
examples.problem: Write 5x + 2y = 2.7 and 3y = 5 in the standard form ax + by + c = 0, and state the values of a, b and c in each case.
steps: For 5x + 2y = 2.7, move every term to one side: 5x + 2y - 2.7 = 0.
Read off a = 5, b = 2 and c = -2.7.
Multiplying by -1 gives -5x - 2y + 2.7 = 0, equally valid with a = -5, b = -2, c = 2.7.
For 3y = 5, write 3y - 5 = 0, or 0 times x + 3y - 5 = 0, so a = 0, b = 3 and c = 5.

examples.title: Testing ordered pairs
examples.problem: Check which of the pairs (2, 3), (4, 0), (1, 3), (0, 6) and (4, 1) are solutions of the equation 3x + 2y = 12.
steps: (2, 3): 3 times 2 + 2 times 3 = 6 + 6 = 12, so it satisfies the equation.
(4, 0): 3 times 4 + 2 times 0 = 12 + 0 = 12, so it is also a solution.
(1, 3): 3 times 1 + 2 times 3 = 9, which is not 12, so it is not a solution.
(0, 6): 3 times 0 + 2 times 6 = 12, a solution; but (4, 1): 3 times 4 + 2 times 1 = 14, not a solution.

examples.title: Substitution method, Example 7
examples.problem: Solve the pair of equations 7x - 15y = 2 and x + 2y = 3 by the substitution method.
steps: Step 1: from the equation x + 2y = 3, express x in terms of y: x = 3 - 2y.
Step 2: substitute x = 3 - 2y into the other equation: 7(3 - 2y) - 15y = 2.
Step 3: put y = 19/29 back into x = 3 - 2y: x = 3 - 38/29 = 49/29.
Verify by substituting x = 49/29 and y = 19/29 into both original equations; both are satisfied.

examples.title: Graphical method, Example 11
examples.problem: Solve the pair of linear equations x + 3y = 6 and 2x - 3y = 12 graphically, and comment on the nature of the solution.
steps: Rewrite the first equation as y = (6 - x)/3; for x = 0 and then 6 we get y = 2 and 0, giving the points (0, 2) and (6, 0).
Rewrite the second equation as y = (2x - 12)/3; for x = 0 and then 3 we get y = -4 and -2, giving the points (0, -4) and (3, -2).
Plot A (0, 2), B (6, 0), P (0, -4) and Q (3, -2) on graph paper and draw the lines AB and PQ.
The lines AB and PQ intersect at B (6, 0), the one point common to both lines.
examples.answer: The solution is x = 6 and y = 0; since the lines meet in a single point, the pair has a unique solution.

flowchart.title: How to crack a pair of linear equations

steps.label: Spot two unknowns
steps.detail: A situation like Radha's cart has two changing quantities.

steps.label: Name x and y
steps.detail: Let x be kilograms of mangoes and y kilograms of bananas.

steps.label: Form the equations
steps.detail: Translate the words into equations like 60x + 50y = 280.

steps.label: Tidy to standard form
steps.detail: Write ax + by + c = 0 and read off a, b and c.

steps.label: Choose a method
steps.detail: Substitution, elimination, or the graphical method.

steps.label: Reduce to one variable
steps.detail: Substitute x = 3 - 2y, or eliminate one variable.

steps.label: Solve and back-substitute
steps.detail: Get y = 19/29, then x = 49/29 as in Example 7.

steps.label: Verify the pair
steps.detail: Check that the ordered pair satisfies both original equations.

steps.label: Or plot both lines
steps.detail: Two tables of values, two lines, and their crossing point is the solution.
